title: Shubman Gill Backs Manav Suthar as India's Long-Term All-Rounder Solution for Sri Lanka Tests
excerpt: The India captain sees the 23-year-old left-arm spinner as a genuine No. 8, filling the all-rounder gap left by Washington Sundar's injury ahead of the two-match Test series in Sri Lanka.
body:
• India captain Shubman Gill has backed 23-year-old left-arm spinner Manav Suthar as a long-term all-rounder option at No. 8 for the Test series against Sri Lanka.
  • Suthar impressed on his Test debut against Afghanistan in June, claiming seven wickets and scoring a valuable 28 to earn the Player of the Match award.
  • With Washington Sundar ruled out through injury, India are deploying a three-spinner attack of Ravindra Jadeja, Kuldeep Yadav, and Suthar for spinning conditions in Galle and Colombo.
  • Jasprit Bumrah has also been ruled out of the series with a left knee injury, with Jammu and Kashmir's Auqib Nabi earning a maiden call-up as his replacement.

India captain Shubman Gill has identified Manav Suthar as the answer to the team's all-rounder gap ahead of the two-match Test series against Sri Lanka, backing the 23-year-old Rajasthan spinner to fill the No. 8 role that has been a persistent selection puzzle.

Why Suthar Fits the All-Rounder Slot

With Washington Sundar ruled out through injury, India needed a spin-bowling all-rounder who could bat with purpose in the lower order. Suthar, a left-arm orthodox spinner, made a compelling case on his Test debut against Afghanistan in June at Chandigarh. He claimed seven wickets in the match and scored a useful 28, earning the Player of the Match award in India's dominant victory.

"Manav Suthar has the potential to be a really good No. 8," Gill said ahead of the series, according to Cricbuzz. The captain's endorsement signals that India's team management sees Suthar as more than a specialist bowler — his batting ability at No. 8 gives the team the kind of lower-order depth that has been missing since the retirements of R Ashwin and the injury-enforced absences of Sundar.

India's Spin Arsenal for Sri Lanka

The two-Test series, which began on August 15 in Galle, represents India's most spin-heavy selection in recent memory. Ravindra Jadeja, returning after sitting out the Afghanistan Test, joins Kuldeep Yadav and Suthar in a three-pronged spin attack tailored for Sri Lanka's turning surfaces.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=VhxIiXhiE0o

Head coach Gautam Gambhir had hinted at this approach before the Afghanistan Test. "This is perhaps the only Test match where we can have a look at someone who could be our fourth spinner," Gambhir told reporters. "Because after this, we go to Sri Lanka, and we might have to carry four spinners."

Suthar also used the gap between series productively, joining Warwickshire for two County Championship matches in England — his first competitive cricket on English soil — before linking up with the squad in Sri Lanka.

Squad Changes: Bumrah Out, Nabi In

India's squad for the series has been reshaped by injuries. Jasprit Bumrah, initially named in the 15-member squad, was ruled out due to a left knee injury sustained during the ODI series against England. The BCCI named Jammu and Kashmir fast bowler Auqib Nabi as his replacement. The 26-year-old earned his maiden national call-up on the strength of 104 wickets across two Ranji Trophy seasons, including 60 in J&K's title-winning 2025-26 campaign.

Top-order batter Sai Sudharsan was also ruled out with injury, with Mumbai's Sarfaraz Khan recalled after a two-year absence.

"He has been absolutely fine. The way he batted in the second inning was again flawless. He is very much ready for the Test match."

— Sairaj Bahutule, India Spin Bowling Coach, on Gill's fitness

What's at Stake

India sit fifth in the ICC World Test Championship standings with a points percentage of 48.15, needing strong results in Sri Lanka to stay in contention for the final. The first Test began in Galle on August 15, with the second scheduled for Colombo from August 23-27. For Suthar, it is an opportunity to cement his place in India's Test setup for years to come.
